fields.summary: Course index subsections expose duplicate treeitem roles

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: Subsection
components.description: Issues related to mod_subsection

fields.description:
Problem statement:
Subsections in the course index currently expose a nested treeitem role. The wrapper for a subsection is exposed as a treeitem even though its parent course-index list item already represents that same subsection as a treeitem. This can cause assistive technologies to perceive two tree nodes for one visible subsection.

This affects people who navigate the course index with assistive technology, particularly screen-reader users. It does not provide a clear, programmatically determinable representation of the subsection as required by WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 4.1.2, Name, Role, Value (Level A).

Current behaviour:
- A visible subsection can be represented by nested elements that both expose role="treeitem".
- Assistive technology may announce or expose duplicate tree nodes for one subsection.
- The attached reference image, MDL-88949-current-behaviour.png, reproduces the duplicate role in the current Moodle main behaviour.

Reference image captured from current behaviour:
!MDL-88949-current-behaviour.png!

Expected behaviour:
- Each visible subsection is exposed as one course-index tree node with one treeitem role.
- The subsection tree node has the correct accessible name.
- Expandable subsection nodes expose the correct expanded or collapsed state.
- Course-index keyboard navigation and subsection expand/collapse behaviour continue to work.

Value:
The course index will expose an unambiguous structure to assistive technologies. Screen-reader users will encounter one meaningful tree node per visible subsection and receive the correct name and state information.

Scope:
In scope:
- The semantic representation of subsection entries in the course index.
- Subsection accessible names, expanded/collapsed states, and existing keyboard interaction as affected by this correction.

Out of scope:
- Other course-index item types.
- The content and presentation of the subsection page itself.
- Unrelated changes to course-index navigation or visual design.

Acceptance criteria:
- A subsection is represented by exactly one treeitem in the browser accessibility tree.
- The subsection treeitem has an accessible name that identifies the subsection.
- A subsection that can expand or collapse exposes the correct aria-expanded state, and that state updates when the subsection is expanded or collapsed.
- Keyboard navigation through the course index continues to include each subsection once and remains functional.
- A screen reader does not announce two tree nodes for a single visible subsection.
- The correction applies whether the subsection is expanded or collapsed and whether it contains course activities.
- Existing course-index display and interaction for subsection entries are unchanged visually.
- Other course-index item types continue to behave as before.

References:
- WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 4.1.2, Name, Role, Value: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html
- WAI-ARIA Tree View Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/
- Current-behaviour reproduction and Firefox DOM evidence: MDL-88949-current-behaviour.png, attached to this issue.

Notes:
The required outcome is one programmatically exposed tree node per visible subsection. The ticket intentionally does not prescribe which HTML element must carry the treeitem role; implementation should follow the established course-index pattern while producing the required accessibility-tree result.

fields.summary: Assignment grading: Sticky table header is misplaced at 400% zoom

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: Assignment
components.description: The new mod_assign module available since Moodle 2.3

fields.description:
Summary:    
At 400% browser zoom and a very short viewport, the sticky header in the assignment submissions grading table stays pinned after the primary navbar is no longer fixed. This leaves a large sticky header consuming much of the viewport, so only a small strip remains for the submission rows.

Problem statement:    
Teachers reviewing assignment submissions at high zoom can lose usable space for the grading table. The problem occurs when the effective viewport is both narrower than 576 CSS pixels and 320 CSS pixels high or less. At this size, the primary navbar is no longer fixed, creating additional vertical space, but the sticky grading-table header keeps occupying a large part of the viewport. Combined with the page sticky footer, very little of the submission table body remains visible.

This is an accessibility defect affecting users who rely on browser zoom and small effective viewports. It relates to WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.10 Reflow (Level AA):  
[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

Current behaviour:

* At 400% zoom, with window.innerWidth at or below 576 pixels and window.innerHeight at or below 320 pixels, the primary navbar is no longer fixed.
* The assignment submissions grading-table header stays sticky and continues to occupy a large part of the small viewport.
* As the teacher scrolls vertically, the sticky header keeps consuming viewport height that is needed for the submission rows.
* When the page sticky footer is also shown, barely any of the submission table body remains readable.
* See the attached reference mockup image image-20260626-041105.png, which must remain attached to this issue.

Expected behaviour:

* When the primary navbar is no longer fixed at the affected viewport size, the assignment submissions grading-table header becomes non-sticky (position: static) so it no longer consumes a large part of the available viewport.
* The header scrolls together with the submission rows, like an ordinary table header, instead of remaining pinned.
* Submission rows remain readable and are not reduced to a small strip beneath a sticky header, including when the page sticky footer is shown.
* Horizontal and vertical scrolling remain available so all grading-table content can be reached at 400% zoom.
* At viewport sizes above the affected breakpoint, the header keeps its normal sticky behaviour.

Value:

Teachers using high browser zoom can read assignment submission data without a sticky header consuming a substantial part of the available viewport. This supports reflow accessibility requirements.

Scope:    
In scope:

* The sticky header used by the assignment submissions grading table.
* Behaviour when the primary navbar is no longer fixed at the affected effective viewport dimensions.
* Equivalent fixes on main, Moodle 5.2, Moodle 5.1, and Moodle 4.5.

Out of scope:

* Sticky headers outside the assignment submissions grading table.
* General redesign of Moodle responsive navigation.
* Changes to assignment grading workflows unrelated to the sticky-header position.

Acceptance criteria:

* At 400% browser zoom, when window.innerWidth is at or below 576 pixels and window.innerHeight is at or below 320 pixels, the assignment submissions grading-table header is non-sticky (position: static) after the primary navbar is no longer fixed, so it does not consume a large part of the viewport.
* At this viewport size the header scrolls with the submission rows rather than remaining pinned.
* Submission rows remain readable and are not left in a small strip beneath a sticky header, including when the page sticky footer is shown.
* All grading-table content remains reachable using horizontal and vertical scrolling.
* Behaviour at viewport dimensions above the affected breakpoint does not regress; the header remains sticky with its normal offset.
* The fix is verified on main, Moodle 5.2, Moodle 5.1, and Moodle 4.5.

Attachments and references:

* image-20260626-041105.png is the reference mockup demonstrating the defect and must remain attached.
* backup-moodle2-course-3-cc101-20250504-0144.mbz provides a course with multiple submissions for testing.
* In the restored course, use the assignment named Cloud-Based Application Design and Deployment.
* Source: 2026 WCAG accessibility audit.

Development branches:

* Main: main_MDL-88955 (already created)
* Moodle 5.2: MOODLE_502_STABLE_MDL-88955 from MOODLE_502_STABLE
* Moodle 5.1: MOODLE_501_STABLE_MDL-88955 from MOODLE_501_STABLE
* Moodle 4.5: MOODLE_405_STABLE_MDL-88955 from MOODLE_405_STABLE
* Push equivalent patches to all four issue branches.
* After pushing, update and verify the Jira repository, branch, and diff URL fields for main, 5.2, 5.1, and 4.5.

fields.summary: Accessibility issues with the custom fields admin pages

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: Custom fields
components.description: Workplace team assume responsibility for this component

fields.description:
Summary:
Ensure that adding a custom field category produces an accessible status message.

Problem statement:
When an administrator adds a category on either of the reported custom fields administration pages, Moodle displays confirmation of the result visually, but the message is not programmatically exposed as a status message. Screen reader users therefore receive no feedback that the category was added.

This affects administrators and other authorised users who use screen readers or comparable assistive technologies.

Current behaviour:
Activating "Add a new category" adds the category and displays visual feedback. Assistive technology does not announce the result.

The problem occurs on:
- Site administration > Courses > Default settings > Course custom fields
- Site administration > General > Custom fields > Shared custom fields

Expected behaviour:
After "Add a new category" is activated, the result is programmatically determinable as a status message and can be announced by assistive technologies without the message receiving focus.

The announcement must provide enough context for the user to understand that a category was added. The existing visual experience must remain available.

Value:
Screen reader users receive equivalent confirmation of the result of their action and can continue working without searching the page for an unannounced change. This addresses WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA).

Scope:
In scope:
- The result of activating "Add a new category" on the Course custom fields administration page.
- The result of activating "Add a new category" on the Shared custom fields administration page.
- Programmatic exposure of the result to assistive technologies.
- Preservation of the existing visual feedback and category-creation behaviour.

Out of scope:
- Other custom field actions, including editing, deleting, reordering, or moving categories or fields.
- Other administration pages.
- General redesign of custom field management.

Acceptance criteria:
- Activating "Add a new category" successfully creates a category on each of the two reported pages.
- The resulting confirmation is programmatically determinable as a status message through an appropriate role or property.
- Assistive technology can announce the complete, meaningful result without focus being moved to the message.
- The message does not use an unnecessarily interruptive alert mechanism for routine success feedback.
- Existing visual confirmation remains visible.
- Existing keyboard focus and category-management behaviour do not regress.

Accessibility reference:
WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages:
https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html

Notes:
WCAG identifies a success or result message which does not change context as a status message. Its sufficient techniques include exposing routine success feedback using role="status". Equivalent conforming implementations are acceptable; the requirement is the observable and programmatic accessibility outcome, not a prescribed implementation.

fields.summary: Accessibility issues in Comments

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
Problem statement

The core comments component (public/comment/comment.js) has two categories of WCAG 2.2 non-compliance affecting all users who post or interact with comments across Moodle.


Colour contrast (SC 1.4.3 Contrast Minimum, Level AA)

1. New comment highlight -- when a comment is submitted, a YUI2 animation permanently sets the newly posted comment's background colour to #FFE390 (yellow) and the text/link colour to #06e (blue). The measured contrast ratio of #0066EE against #FFE390 is 4.02:1, below the required 4.5:1 minimum for normal-weight text. Any grey meta text rendered over the same yellow background has a contrast ratio of only 3.13:1. The yellow background persists indefinitely after the animation completes.

The attached screenshots show both issues in context.

User link on yellow background: !image-20260625-085115.png|thumbnail!

Comment date and text on yellow background: !image-20260625-085132.png|thumbnail!

2. Simulated placeholder text -- the comment textarea uses a JavaScript placeholder simulation (toggle_textarea in comment.js) that sets the textarea value to the string "Add a comment" and styles it with colour grey (#808080). The contrast ratio of #808080 against a white background is 3.95:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum.


Use of colour (SC 1.4.1, Level A)

The animation at comment.js line 107 sets the colour of the entire newly posted comment list item -- including both the username anchor element and the surrounding non-link text -- to #06e. Because both link and non-link content receive the same colour, and no independent non-colour visual indicator (such as an underline) is separately enforced for the link in that state, colour becomes the only visual means of distinguishing the username link from surrounding text.


Current behaviour

When a comment is posted, the new list item permanently receives background #FFE390 and text/link colour #06e via a YUI2 ColorAnim call. The textarea placeholder is simulated by setting its value to the "Add a comment" string in grey. Neither colour choice meets WCAG 2.2 Level AA contrast requirements. The username link is not visually distinguishable from surrounding text during the highlighted state.


Expected behaviour

All text and interactive controls within the comments component must meet SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) AA (4.5:1 for normal-weight text). The username link must have a non-colour visual indicator. The textarea placeholder text must be implemented in a way that meets contrast requirements.


WCAG references

- SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) Level AA: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html
- SC 1.4.1 Use of Color Level A: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/use-of-color.html


Design system tokens

The Moodle Design System (@moodlehq/design-system) does not include a direct equivalent to #FFE390. The closest available semantic token for a new-item highlight background is:

- $mds-bg-feedback-warning-subtle: #fcefdc (contrast 7.82:1 with $mds-text-feedback-warning, 14.28:1 with $mds-text-default, 4.73:1 with $mds-text-link-primary-default -- all pass AA)

For the placeholder text, suitable tokens include:

- $mds-text-subtle: #495057 (contrast 8.18:1 on white -- passes AAA)
- $mds-text-muted: #6a737b (contrast 4.83:1 on white -- passes AA)


Scope

In scope:
- Contrast and use-of-colour fixes for the new comment highlight animation in public/comment/comment.js
- Contrast fix for the textarea placeholder colour in public/comment/comment.js

Out of scope:
- Accessibility improvements to other comment implementations (e.g. mod/assign/feedback/comments, mod/workshop/form/comments)
- Structural refactoring of the YUI2-based comment system


Value

These are Level A and AA WCAG 2.2 failures that affect every Moodle user who posts or reads comments across the platform. Resolving them is a prerequisite for WCAG conformance claims and directly affects users with low vision or colour-perception difficulties.


Acceptance criteria

1. Text and link content within a newly posted comment that has received the highlight background colour meets SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) AA (4.5:1) for normal-weight text.
2. The username link within a highlighted new comment has a non-colour visual indicator distinguishing it as a link (e.g. underline), satisfying SC 1.4.1.
3. The textarea placeholder text meets SC 1.4.3 AA (4.5:1) contrast against its background.
4. Where design system tokens are available for the chosen colours, they are used in preference to hardcoded hex values.
5. All fixes are applied to main, MOODLE_502_STABLE, and MOODLE_501_STABLE.

fields.summary: Activity chooser: Filter tabs don't reflow at 400% zoom (WCAG 1.4.10)

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
h3. Problem statement

On the Activity chooser page, when the viewport is narrow (e.g. 320x256 pixels, equivalent to 400% zoom on a standard 1280x1024 display), the content fails to reflow. The category filter tabs and the activity list do not adapt to the narrow viewport, and the fixed search header and footer occupy most of the available space. This is a violation of WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 (Reflow): https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html

h3. Who is affected

Any user with permission to add an activity or resource (e.g. teacher, course creator, manager, admin) who opens the Activity chooser, including users who rely on browser zoom or small viewports for accessibility reasons.

h3. Current behaviour

At 320x256 / 400% zoom, the Activity chooser does not reflow correctly:

* The search header and category filter tabs remain fixed/sticky at the top, consuming most of the vertical viewport.
* The footer remains fixed at the bottom with its current padding, further reducing usable space.
* Category tabs and activities do not stack, making the content impossible to read or use without horizontal scrolling.

See the attached screenshot below (image-20260624-083427.png) showing the problem at 400% zoom:

!image-20260624-083427.png|width=1174,alt="image-20260624-083427.png"!

h3. Expected behaviour

* The search header and category filter tabs should no longer be sticky/fixed; they should scroll up and out of the viewport with the rest of the page content. Their vertical padding should be reduced to give more room to the content below.
* The footer should remain sticky, but with reduced vertical padding so it takes up less of the viewport and leaves more room for content.
* Activity categories should stack vertically, one underneath the other, instead of being shown as horizontal tabs.
* Activities within a category should stack in a single column (one per row) underneath their category, rather than in a grid.
* See the attached mockup image category_example.png for the target category layout. Note: in that mockup the activities themselves are shown as rows of two — this is incorrect and must be implemented as rows of one (single column) instead, per the point above.

h3. Value

Fixes a WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 (Reflow) accessibility failure, allowing users who rely on browser zoom or small/narrow viewports to read and use the Activity chooser without loss of content or functionality and without horizontal scrolling.

h3. Scope

In scope:

* Activity chooser reflow at 320x256 viewport / 400% zoom equivalent.
* Making the search header and category tabs non-sticky, with reduced padding.
* Reducing footer padding while keeping it sticky.
* Stacking category tabs vertically.
* Stacking activities in a single column under their category.

Out of scope:

* Any other page or component reflow not related to the Activity chooser.
* Changes to activity chooser search/filter logic or functionality beyond layout/reflow.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* At a 320x256 viewport (or 400% zoom on a 1280x1024 display), the search header and category tabs scroll out of view with the page instead of remaining fixed, with reduced vertical padding.
* At the same viewport, the footer remains sticky but with reduced vertical padding.
* Category tabs are displayed stacked vertically, one under the other.
* Activities are displayed stacked in a single column (one per row) under their category.
* No horizontal scrolling or content clipping occurs at this viewport.
* Keyboard focus order remains logical after the layout changes to stacked categories/activities.
* Normal desktop-width behaviour (e.g. 1280x1024, no zoom) is unchanged.

h3. Notes

* This is an accessibility bug (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 - Reflow).
* Original GrackleDocs finding: when zoomed to 400%, the page content is impossible to read as the fixed search header and footer occupy most of the viewport.
* Reference mockup for the category layout is attached as category_example.png. The activity layout in that mockup (rows of two) is not correct and must be implemented as rows of one instead.
* This bug requires patches on multiple supported Moodle versions (main, and the two most recent stable branches) in addition to main.
* See the Testing Instructions field on this issue for detailed step-by-step verification steps.

fields.summary: Glossary "Browse by alphabet" does not work for Cyrillic entries in Moodle 5.x

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
The Glossary "Browse by alphabet" feature does not correctly display entries that start with Cyrillic characters.

The glossary entry is stored correctly in the database and the correct Cyrillic letter is passed in the URL parameter ({{hook}}), but no entries are displayed.

The same glossary works correctly in Moodle 4.4.

This appears to be a regression introduced after Moodle 4.4.

Root cause analysis

The issue appears to be caused by UTF-8 handling in:

mod/glossary/lib.php

function:

glossary_get_entries_by_letter()

Current implementation:

{noformat}if (strtoupper(substr(format_string($entry->concept), 0, 1)) === strtoupper($letter)) {{noformat}

The code uses PHP {{substr()}}, which operates on bytes rather than UTF-8 characters.

For Cyrillic glossary concepts such as:

Коло

{{substr(..., 0, 1)}} returns only the first byte of the UTF-8 sequence rather than the complete character.

As a result, the comparison fails and glossary entries are not displayed when browsing by alphabet.

The issue can be resolved by using Moodle UTF-8 aware string functions such as {{core_text::substr()}} and {{core_text::strtoupper()}}.

h1. Steps to reproduce

{noformat}1. Create a glossary activity.
2. Add an entry with concept "Коло".
3. Open the glossary.
4. Select "Browse by alphabet".
5. Click the letter "К".{noformat}

----

h1. Expected result

{noformat}The glossary should display the entry:

Коло{noformat}

----

h1. Actual result

{noformat}The glossary displays:

"No entries found in this section"

even though the entry exists in the glossary.{noformat}

----

h1. Additional information

The URL contains the correct Cyrillic letter:

{noformat}.../mod/glossary/view.php?id=22&mode=letter&hook=%D0%9A{noformat}

which is decoded as:

{noformat}К{noformat}

fields.summary: Allow column::add_fields() to accept array of field strings

components.name: Report builder

fields.description:
*Note:* *This ticket was created by an AI agent (GitHub Copilot)*

h2. Proposal: Union Type for column::add_fields()

h3. Current State

The {{add_fields()}} method in {{public/reportbuilder/classes/local/report/column.php}} accepts only a comma-separated string of fields. Internally it uses {{preg_split()}} to split the string back into individual fields. Some call sites have multiple fields to add, requiring them to use {{implode()}} before calling the method:

{code:php}->add_fields(implode(", ", [
    "{$tablealias}.id",
    "{$tablealias}.name",
    // ...
])){code}

This creates a redundant {{implode()}} then {{preg_split()}} round-trip.

h3. Proposal

Allow {{add_fields()}} to accept either a string *or* an array of field strings ({{string|array}}), enabling callers to pass arrays directly:

{code:php}->add_fields([
    "{$tablealias}.id",
    "{$tablealias}.name",
    // ...
]){code}

Each array element uses the same field syntax as the string format — {{table.field}}, {{table.field alias}}, or {{table.field AS alias}}.

h3. Affected Call Sites

Two instances in the codebase currently use the {{implode()}} pattern:

* {{public/reportbuilder/classes/local/systemreports/reports_list.php}} (line 129)
* {{public/webservice/classes/reportbuilder/local/systemreports/tokens.php}} (line 140)

h3. Benefits

* Cleaner, more readable call-site code
* Eliminates redundant string joining/parsing
* More intuitive API for callers with multiple fields
* Fully backward compatible — existing string calls are unaffected

fields.summary: Hardcoded dependencies on AI plugins breaks the site if they are uninstalled

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: AI
components.description: Issues related to the LMS AI Subsystem

fields.description:
Summary:
Prevent optional AI placement plugins from breaking core course forms when they are uninstalled.

Problem statement:
Core course-management code directly calls utility classes from the optional aiplacement_courseassist and aiplacement_editor plugins. If either plugin is uninstalled, the corresponding class is unavailable and opening the affected course or activity form can fail with a missing-class error.

Affected direct dependencies:

* public/course/edit_form.php: aiplacement_courseassist\utils::is_course_assist_available()
* public/course/edit_form.php: aiplacement_editor\utils::is_html_editor_placement_available()
* public/course/modlib.php: aiplacement_courseassist\utils::get_actions_available($PAGE->context, false)
* public/course/modlib.php: aiplacement_editor\utils::get_actions_available($PAGE->context, false)
* public/course/moodleform_mod.php: aiplacement_courseassist\utils::is_course_assist_available()
* public/course/moodleform_mod.php: aiplacement_courseassist\utils::get_actions_available($this->get_context(), false)
* public/course/moodleform_mod.php: aiplacement_editor\utils::is_html_editor_placement_available()
* public/course/moodleform_mod.php: aiplacement_editor\utils::get_actions_available($this->get_context(), false)

Current behaviour:
On a site where either optional AI placement plugin has been uninstalled, a user can encounter a fatal error when opening affected course or activity editing workflows. The failure was introduced as part of the AI access-controls work in MDL-85738.

Expected behaviour:
Core course and activity workflows must continue to load when either optional AI placement plugin is not installed. AI controls and actions must continue to be shown only when their relevant placement is installed and available.

Architectural requirement:
aiplacement components are plugins and therefore optional. In line with Moodle's component-communication policy, core course code must not directly reference, load, or call a named placement plugin class, including behind a placement-specific class_exists() or equivalent guard.

The core AI subsystem provides the component-neutral integration point. Course code calls its manager API, which discovers installed and enabled AI placement plugins and obtains their context-specific availability and actions through the common core AI placement API. This discovery mechanism is an internal concern of the core AI subsystem; it does not require each placement plugin to implement a lib.php callback. Each placement owns its placement-specific availability, capability, and action behaviour. This keeps core course code independent of any particular placement and lets an optional placement be removed without changing core code.

Value:
Administrators can choose which optional AI placements to install without risking a site-breaking error in core course-management workflows.

Scope:

* Replace the direct dependencies listed above with the component-neutral core AI manager API.
* Preserve existing AI behaviour when the corresponding placement plugin is installed.
* Support main, Moodle 5.2.1, and Moodle 5.1.6.

Out of scope:

* Changing AI access-control rules or placement behaviour when all relevant plugins are installed.
* Requiring either optional placement plugin to remain installed.
* Adding a dependency from core course code to a specific placement plugin.

Acceptance criteria:

* Uninstalling aiplacement_courseassist does not cause an error when opening or editing a course or activity.
* Uninstalling aiplacement_editor does not cause an error when opening or editing a course or activity.
* Course code has no placement-specific direct class or utility calls; it uses the component-neutral core AI manager API.
* Core AI placement discovery excludes uninstalled and disabled placements.
* When a placement is installed and available, its existing course or editor AI controls and actions remain available according to current capability and availability checks.
* Automated regression coverage covers both installed and uninstalled placement cases.

Notes:

* This is a regression from MDL-85738 in the Moodle 5.1 series.
* This implementation must follow the Moodle component-communication policy.

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Improvement

components.name: Feedback
components.description: The Feedback module, useful for surveying.

fields.description:
With the introduction of the core course linear navigation feature, which uses a text-based sticky footer ("Previous" / "Next") to cycle through course activities, the current layout of the mod_feedback response view introduces user experience friction:

!image-20260701-125253.png|width=600,alt="image-20260701-125253.png"!

To resolve this ambiguity, we will refactor the report navigation UX by replacing text links with compact, icon-only pagination buttons, as in the forum activity. We will add a sticky footer with a "Go to all responses" link, also like the forum. Using distinct chevrons clearly isolates the interaction to "navigating records within this report" rather than "moving to the next course activity":

!image-20260701-125348.png|width=600,alt="image-20260701-125348.png"!



h3. 🎯 Required actions

* Extract the text-based "◄ Prev", "Back", and "Next ►" action links from the feedback show responses view layout.
* Implement sticky footer: Call the {{set_supplementary_content()}} method to display the “Go to all responses” link.
* Replace textual pagination with standard core chevron icon components, with localised screen-reader text (aria-label), to ensure strict visual differentiation from primary course navigation text buttons.
* Update the relevant output renderers and mustache templates (within mod_feedback) to leverage core UI components and utility classes instead of inline or legacy structural styling.

h3. (/) Acceptance criteria

* The legacy text navigation links ("◄ Prev", "Back", "Next ►") are completely removed from the view.
* A sticky footer is implemented and anchors correctly at the bottom of the viewport.
* The page contains functional, rounded chevron/arrow buttons for "Previous" and "Next" records where applicable, eliminating text-based pagination controls.
* Accessibility compliance is maintained by applying localised aria-label attributes to the new icon controls (e.g., "Previous response", "Next response") so screen readers can clearly disambiguate them from course activity navigation.
* A "Go to all responses" link is centred within the sticky footer area and correctly redirects back to the response overview table.

----

fields.description:
When linear navigation is enabled in supported course formats, Moodle renders a sticky footer with Previous/Next controls on activity pages. Portfolio export pages are workflow pages (selection/configuration/export) and are not part of activity-to-activity progression. The sticky footer should therefore not be shown on portfolio pages.

At the moment, the sticky footer can appear in portfolio flows, introducing unrelated controls and inconsistent UX. This should be aligned with existing MDL-84921 suppressions on non-learning-flow pages.

*Steps to reproduce:*

# Enable portfolios in Advanced features.
# Enable at least one portfolio plugin instance.
# Enable linear navigation in a supported course format (e.g. Topics/Weeks).
# Open an activity that supports portfolio export (Forum, Glossary, Database, Assignment, Workshop).
# Click Export to portfolio.
# Observe the sticky linear navigation footer on portfolio page(s).

🎯 *Expected result:*
No linear navigation sticky footer is displayed on any portfolio page.

h3. (/) *Acceptance criteria*

* Given linear navigation is enabled, when a user is on any core portfolio export page, then the linear navigation sticky footer is not displayed.
* Existing linear navigation behavior on normal activity pages is unchanged.
* Portfolio export workflow (instance selection, configuration, export completion/return) works as before.
* Automated coverage exists (new or updated) to verify footer suppression on portfolio pages.

fields.description:
During the recent redesign of the navigation buttons in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88600|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88600|smart-link], the strings for the disabled buttons were updated to be different from their enabled counterparts.

However, while working on [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89068|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89068|smart-link] to add similar buttons to the feedback activity, it was decided to align the approach across both components to ensure accessibility and consistency. Instead of using unique strings when navigation buttons are disabled, we will reuse the exact same {{aria-label}} strings used when the buttons are *enabled*. Screen readers will automatically append or announce the "disabled" state based on the button's HTML attribute ({{aria-disabled="true"}}), making the unique text redundant and ensuring a consistent user experience.



h3. 🎯 *Required actions*

* Locate and remove the unique localisation strings/keys introduced in [MDL-88600|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88600] for the disabled state of the forum response navigation icons.
* Update the forum response navigation buttons so that they reference the standard, enabled {{aria-label}} strings regardless of their active/disabled state.
* Review the automated tests and adapt them properly

h3. (/) *Acceptance criteria*

* The unique localisation strings for the "disabled" navigation icons are completely removed from the codebase (they don’t need to be deprecated).
* When a response navigation button is disabled, its {{aria-label}} matches the enabled button's {{aria-label}} exactly.
* When a response navigation button is enabled, the title appears; it hides when the button is disabled.
* Screen readers (e.g., NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) successfully announce the button's purpose _and_ clearly state that it is currently "disabled" or "diminished."
* No regression is introduced to the navigation functionality itself.

fields.description:
Currently, {{public/lib/js/esm/src/String.tsx}} mixes two concerns in a single file:

# Plain TypeScript utilities for fetching, batching, and caching language strings ({{getRequestedStrings}}, {{getStrings}}, {{cacheStrings}}, {{getString}}, {{resetStringCache}}, and the {{StringParams}}/{{StringRequest}}/{{CacheStringEntry}} types).
# A React component ({{<String>}}) that wraps {{getString}} with {{Suspense}}/{{use()}} for JSX consumption.

This means any code that only needs the string-fetching logic (e.g. non-React modules, or unit tests) is forced to pull in a {{.tsx}} file with a React dependency.

This change extracts the pure-TypeScript logic into a new module, {{public/lib/js/esm/src/stringUtils.ts}}, with no functional changes. {{String.tsx}} now imports from {{stringUtils.ts}} and keeps only the React component ({{StringInner}}/{{<String>}}).

Since this API was only introduced in {{main}} and has not shipped in any release, it is not subject to backwards-compatibility requirements. All known callers have been updated to import directly from {{@moodle/lms/core/stringUtils}} instead of going through {{@moodle/lms/core/String}}:

* {{public/lib/js/esm/src/deprecated.ts}}
* {{public/lib/js/esm/tests/String.test.tsx}}
* {{.jest/globalSetup.ts}}
* {{public/lib/amd/src/str.js}} (the AMD {{core/str}} backward-compatibility shim, which loads the ESM module via {{core/esm!@moodle/lms/core/stringUtils}})

{{@moodle/lms/core/String}} no longer re-exports the string-fetching utilities — it exports only the {{<String>}} component and {{StringProps}}.

fields.description:
To support an internal OAuth2 authorisation server within Moodle, we need a centralised management class to handle CRUD operations for OAuth2 clients, their associated secrets, and redirect URIs.

Scope:

* The class should implement methods that allow
** Fetching clients
*** by ID
*** by client identifier
** Updating a client (restricted to modifying administrative metadata: name, description)
** Revoking a client
** Reactivating a revoked client
** Permanent deletion of a client
** Generation of client secrets (including a logic to enforce a maximum active secret limit per user to 2)
** Fetching client secrets
** Revoking client secrets
** Fetching redirect URIs
** Creation of redirect URIs
** Removal of redirect URIs
** Validation of redirect URIs
* Unit test coverage

h2. Clarifications

* *Secret limit scope*: the maximum of 2 active secrets is enforced *per client*, not per user (a user may own multiple clients, each with its own limit of 2 active secrets).
* *Client revocation cascade*: revoking a client immediately revokes all of that client's active tokens and secrets (integrates with the revocation logic in MDL-88473), fully cutting off access rather than just blocking new token issuance.
* *Reactivation semantics*: reactivating a revoked client only restores the client record itself. Previously-revoked secrets and tokens remain revoked; the client must generate new secrets and go through authorization again to obtain new tokens.
* *Deletion precondition*: permanent deletion is only allowed once a client is already in a revoked state. This acts as a safety guard against accidentally destroying a live integration.
* *Redirect URI validation*: URIs must match exactly (no prefix/wildcard matching) and must use HTTPS, except for {{localhost}}/loopback addresses (to support native app development). No cap on the number of redirect URIs per client.
* *Class design*: all methods must be instance methods (not static), and the class is expected to be loaded via dependency injection (Moodle's {{\core\di}} container), not instantiated directly or accessed via static/singleton patterns.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# All CRUD/lifecycle methods listed above are implemented with the rules described in Clarifications.
# Secret generation enforces the per-client limit of 2 active secrets.
# Revoking a client cascades to revoke its active tokens and secrets.
# Reactivating a client does not restore previously-revoked secrets/tokens.
# Permanent deletion is rejected unless the client is already revoked.
# Redirect URI validation rejects non-exact matches and non-HTTPS URIs (except localhost/loopback).
# The class exposes only instance methods and is resolvable via dependency injection.
# PHPUnit test coverage for all of the above, including edge cases (secret limit exceeded, delete-before-revoke rejection, invalid redirect URI schemes, reactivation not restoring secrets).

----

fields.description:
Design the administrator-facing interface for managing registered OAuth2 clients.

This issue covers the user experience for listing, creating, viewing, editing, rotating credentials for, and deleting OAuth2 clients. It does not cover Personal Access Tokens, the OAuth login page, or the OAuth consent screen.

h2. Audience and access

The initial interface is for site administrators. The design should not prevent access being controlled by capabilities in a future iteration.

h2. Client model

Each client represents one integration or use case. For example, the Moodle mobile app and a server-to-server web-service integration should be represented by separate clients.

A client has an immutable type and primary OAuth2 flow. Administrators must create a new client rather than changing either value after creation.

h2. Client creation

The create flow should guide an administrator through:

# Choosing a client type:
#* Public
#* Confidential
# Choosing a permitted primary OAuth2 flow:
#* Public clients: Authorization Code, without a client secret.
#* Confidential clients: Authorization Code, with a client secret.
#* Confidential clients: Client Credentials, with a client secret.
#* Confidential clients: Resource Owner Password Credentials, with a client secret.

# Completing the relevant client configuration.

The selected client type and flow must be clearly explained during creation, including that they cannot be changed later.

h2. Client configuration

The wireframes should cover creating and editing a client, including:

* Name
* Description
* Icon
* Primary OAuth2 flow
* Client type
* Flow-specific settings
* Valid callback URIs where applicable:
** At least one callback URI is required for redirect-based flows.
** Only HTTPS, {{localhost}}, and {{127.0.0.1}} are permitted.

The design should show only configuration relevant to the selected client type and flow. For example, Client Credentials and Resource Owner Password Credentials clients do not require callback URI configuration.

*Permitted scopes*

Administrators configure the published OAuth scopes that a client is permitted to request.

Known Moodle integrations may begin with a recommended set of permitted scopes, which an administrator can restrict. Administrator-created clients begin with no permitted scopes selected and require explicit selection.

A client may request only a subset of its permitted scopes. The design must show the effect of removing a permitted scope, including that the updated policy applies to future authorisation and refresh activity. Exact token invalidation behaviour is to be confirmed during implementation design.

h2. Client list and details

Design:

* A list of registered clients with relevant identifying and security information, including at least name, client type, primary flow, status, and appropriate access metadata.
* A separate client detail page.
* Actions to edit a client, manage its secrets, and delete the client.
* Clear presentation of immutable fields, particularly client type and primary flow.

h2. Secrets and deletion

Confidential clients have client secrets.

The design must cover:

* Automatically generating a secret.
* Showing a newly generated secret one time only.
* Allowing up to two active secrets to support credential rotation.
* Revoking a secret permanently.
* Relevant metadata for each secret or token where available, including last access time and IP address.

Deleting a client permanently invalidates its active secrets and issued tokens. The design must include a clear confirmation flow for this irreversible action.

h2. Deliverables

Produce low- to medium-fidelity wireframes and supporting notes covering:

* Empty, populated, validation, error, confirmation, and irreversible-action states.
* The primary create, edit, secret rotation/revocation, and delete journeys.
* Any assumptions or unresolved design decisions.
* Accessibility and responsive considerations where they affect the interaction.

h2. Acceptance criteria

* Wireframes show permitted-scope selection in accordance with the OAuth2 administration design.
* The design implements the client type and flow model described above.
* Client type and primary OAuth2 flow are selectable only during creation and are read-only afterwards.
* PKCE is optional for Authorization Code clients and shown only where relevant.
* Public clients do not use client secrets; confidential clients do.
* Flow-specific configuration is shown only where relevant.
* Secret creation, one-time display, rotation, revocation, and client deletion states are clearly represented.
* The design is reviewed and agreed before implementation begins.

fields.description:
Design the user-facing interface for creating and managing Personal Access Tokens (PATs).

This issue covers the self-service PAT interface in user preferences. It does not cover OAuth2 client management, the OAuth login page, or the OAuth consent screen.

h2. Audience and access

Access to PAT management is controlled by a capability.

Users can view and manage only their own PATs.

h2. PAT model

A user may have multiple active tokens.

Each token:

* Has a name and description.
* Has one or more selected scopes.
* Has a mandatory expiry date, no more than one year from its creation date.
* Is immutable after creation. Changing its name, description, expiry date, or scopes requires creating a new token.
* Becomes unusable automatically when it expires, but remains visible as an expired token until the user deletes it.

h2. Location and overview

The PAT interface should be available from user preferences.

Design a single management page that shows all relevant token information and actions without requiring a separate token-details page.

For each token, show at least:

* Name
* Description
* Scopes, with plain-language descriptions
* Created date
* Expiry date
* Last used time where available
* Status: active or expired

The page should provide an action to create a new token and appropriate empty states when the user has no tokens.

h2. Token creation

The create-token flow should allow the user to provide:

* Name
* Description
* Expiry date, validated to be in the future and no more than one year ahead
* One or more scopes

Scope selection should include a short plain-language description of the access granted by each scope. No additional warning is required for broad or sensitive scopes in the first version.

After creating a token:

* Display the token value once only.
* Provide a copy action.
* Clearly explain that the token value cannot be viewed again after leaving or acknowledging this screen.
* Do not reveal the token value in the management list after this point.

h2. Token deletion

Deleting an active token immediately revokes it and removes it from the active-token list.

Expired tokens remain visible until deleted.

The design must include clear confirmation flows for deleting active and expired tokens, making the consequences of deleting an active token explicit.

h2. Deliverables

Produce low- to medium-fidelity wireframes and supporting notes covering:

* The empty and populated token-management page.
* Creating a token, including scope selection and expiry-date validation.
* The one-time token display and copy experience.
* Active and expired token states.
* Deletion confirmation for active and expired tokens.
* Validation, error, and confirmation states.
* Any assumptions or unresolved design decisions.
* Accessibility and responsive considerations where they affect the interaction.

h2. Acceptance criteria

* Wireframes define a self-service PAT management experience in user preferences.
* Access is capability-controlled and users can manage only their own tokens.
* Users can create multiple tokens, each with one or more scopes and a mandatory expiry date of no more than one year.
* Token values are displayed and copyable once only after creation.
* Token settings cannot be changed after creation.
* The main page shows all relevant token metadata, including status, expiry, and available access information.
* Expired tokens remain visible until deleted.
* Deleting an active token revokes it immediately.
* The design is reviewed and agreed before implementation begins.

Whilst working on [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88472|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88472|smart-link] I’ve found a number of minor issues with the login page, renderable, and template.

These issues include:

* when we dropped the boot bootstrap base theme we did not move the login page template from boost to core. Therefore we have two templates, but can only ever use _or test_ the boost variant. The one in core is entirely inaccessible to us, and therefore is a risk
* The {{$hasinstructions}} and {{$instructions}} template/php vars are no longer available
* The renderable is comprised of public properties which are calculated during construct, and never modified. These should be calculated during the export, and not public
* Whilst most values for the renderable are generated _within_ the renderable, a handful are generated _outside_ of it in the renderer, leading to duplication of this calculation logic.

I’m proposing:

# create a new {{loginform}} renderable, whose name matches the existing template - this allows for better backwards/forwards compatibility for plugins who are modifying the login form as they can continue to do so for <=5.2 and have a different way for 5.3+
# move the boost theme to core and remove the core variant
# drop unused parts of the template
# consolidate all of the template vars
# make all of the relevant class properties to be calculated during the export_for_template instead of the constructor and outside of the renderable

Note: This work is a precursor to [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88472|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88472|smart-link].

fields.summary: Drawer toggle/close icons (sidebar_left/sidebar_right) misaligned after SVG browser compatibility fix

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
*Steps to reproduce:*

# Open dashboard/course page.
# Locate the left/right drawer toggle buttons (open course index / open blocks drawer), and the drawer close button once a drawer is open.

*Expected result:*

The sidebar arrow icons ({{e/sidebar_left}} and {{e/sidebar_right}}) are centered inside their buttons.

*Actual result:*

The icons appear slightly shifted to the left.

*Root cause:*

# MDL-88409 updated these icons to use a square {{viewBox="0 0 16 16"}}. However, the space used to display the icons ({{.icon-size-3 .icon}} in {{icons.scss}}) is *20×16*, not square.
# The *"*[*NOBUG: Fixed SVG browser compatibility*|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/commit/30926218ef33aa91363457616b475ba9a04f5177]*"* change added {{preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMid meet"}} to these SVGs to fix a browser compatibility issue. 
The {{xMin}} value aligns the SVG content to the left instead of the center. Because the SVG is *16×16* but the icon container is *20×16*, the icons end up looking slightly left of center.
[https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Reference/Attribute/preserveAspectRatio|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Reference/Attribute/preserveAspectRatio|smart-link] 



Before the "NOBUG: Fixed SVG browser compatibility" commit, the icon is centered:

!Screenshot 2026-07-23 at 06.09.31-20260722-230937.png|width=100,alt="Screenshot 2026-07-23 at 06.09.31-20260722-230937.png"!

After the "NOBUG: Fixed SVG browser compatibility" commit, the icon is shifted slightly to the left:

!Screenshot 2026-07-23 at 06.09.48-20260722-230953.png|width=100,alt="Screenshot 2026-07-23 at 06.09.48-20260722-230953.png"!

fields.description:
{{core/react_string}} requires callers to provide {{children}} as a fallback while the requested string is loading. Where no suitable localised fallback exists, callers must use boilerplate such as:

{code:html}<String identifier="noevents" component="block_timeline">{''}</String>{code}

Make the fallback child optional, defaulting to an empty string. This allows:

{noformat}<String identifier="noevents" component="block_timeline" />{noformat}

Existing callers that provide fallback content must continue to behave unchanged.

*Acceptance criteria:*

* {{children}} is optional in the component’s TypeScript props. 
*  No fallback renders as an empty string while loading. 
*  Existing callers with fallback children continue to work. 
*  Relevant unit tests cover both forms.
